note_sections.t: Ongoing assessment driven by sustained PSA increases and a previous biopsy that identified low-grade malignancy.

Surveillance began after an initial PSA rise in late 2023, and this 73-year-old man now returns for a structured reassessment following a prior biopsy bucket "Positive" and a current PSA of 7.2 ng/mL. He describes moderate lower urinary tract complaints aligning with an IPSS score of 20/35, dominated by nocturia and a diminished stream, though he explicitly denies hematuria or acute retention. He is a 73-year-old, Married man who Lives in assisted-living facility. By occupation, he is a retired truck driver. Active medication: None. Comorbidities: Chronic kidney disease. Current smoker (26 pack-yr). During downtime, he tends to a garden and drinks roughly four units of alcohol weekly. His eGFR has consistently remained under 60 mL/min/1.73m2. A recent dermatology visit addressed routine actinic keratosis screening. A sports-related knee arthroscopy occurred more than ten years ago, leaving him without current mobility restrictions. Former self-employment previously led him to request flexible scheduling.

Digital rectal examination is normal; the prostate exhibits a smooth, firm consistency, symmetric dimensions, and no palpable nodules or asymmetry. Vital signs remain stable, and systemic review shows no abnormalities. Despite residing in an assisted-living setting, he maintains independent ambulation and appears well-nourished.

admin: Patient self-employed; flexible appointment slots requested.
